paragraphs.text: [선택형 7~10] 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 고르시오. [각 1.3점]
7. In the past, the bus came only once an hour, but now it has become so _____________ that we can see one every ten minutes.
① scarce   		② terminal   		③ hesitant
④ frequent  		⑤ absolute
This is not a special or unique problem; in fact, it is a _____________ case that many students experience at least once.
① radical   		② neutral   		③ typical
④ spiritual   		⑤ vague
9. After the students explained why they needed a new club, the principal finally decided to _____________ their plan.
① approve   		② abandon   		③ acquire
④ disguise   		⑤ illustrate
10. The airline provides many international flights, but it is also famous for its _____________ flights that travel between local cities.
① exotic   		② atomic   		③ domestic
④ toxic   		⑤ historic
[선택형 1~5] 다음 해석을 보고, 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 단어를 고르시오. [각 1.1점]
1. The two cases presented to the court were nearly _____________, making it difficult for the jury to reach a distinct verdict.
[법정에 제출된 두 사건은 거의 동일해서, 배심원단이 뚜렷한 평결을 내리기를 어렵게 만들었다.]
① identify   ② independent   ③ instant   ④ incredible   ⑤ identical
2. Many people believe that _____________ greed is one of the main causes of environmental destruction in the modern era.
[많은 사람들이 기업의 탐욕이 현대 사회 환경 파괴의 주요 원인 중 하나라고 믿는다.]
① cooperate   ② incorporate   ③ corporate   ④ operate   ⑤ coordinate
3. To _____________ one’s potential in a competitive environment, one must possess both talent and relentless perseverance.
[경쟁적인 환경에서 자신의 잠재력을 달성하기 위해서, 사람은 재능과 끈질긴 인내력을 모두 갖추어야 한다.]
① extend   ② compose   ③ fulfill   ④ contact   ⑤ generate
4. Adhering to the _____________ of integrity is crucial for maintaining public trust in any democratic institution.
[진실성의 원칙을 고수하는 것은 어떤 민주적 기관에서든 대중의 신뢰를 유지하는 데 중요하다.]
① principal   ② principle   ③ participate   ④ priority   ⑤ possession
5. It is our collective responsibility to _____________ endangered species and their natural habitats for future generations.
[미래 세대를 위해 멸종 위기 종들과 그들의 자연 서식지를 보존하는 것은 우리의 공동 책임이다.]
① persevere   ② deserve   ③ converse   ④ preserve   ⑤ observe
6. In scientific experiments, maintaining a _____________ temperature is crucial to ensure that the results are both reliable and valid.
[과학 실험에서, 결과가 신뢰할 수 있고 타당하다는 것을 보장하기 위해서는 일정한 온도를 유지하는 것이 매우 중요하다.]
① complete     ② instant     ③ resistant     ④ constant     ⑤ concrete
밑줄 친 cognitive misers가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]

There is a natural assumption of truth, or a truth bias when humans communicate with one another. In other words, when we’re listening to others or reading their words, our automatic assumption is that the other person is telling the truth. This usually works out fine. If you ask someone where the restroom is located or if it’s raining outside, you can safely assume that most people will not lie in their responses. Imagine how difficult it would be to converse with someone if you assumed that everything they were telling you was false! Indeed, questioning the truth of a statement and then choosing not to believe it requires additional mental steps. For the most part, humans are “cognitive misers.” It makes sense then, that when we see something online, even if it is fake, our default is to believe it, at least at first.
① People tend to use complex reasoning when facing problems.
② We are easily fooled by false information despite our efforts.
③ Lying leads to errors in how we process information cognitively.
④ Humans always analyze every piece of information before accepting it as true.
⑤ We typically don’t expend more mental effort than seems necessary in a given situation.
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
Science is concerned with accumulating and understanding observations of the physical world.

(A) Knowing this fact is interesting, but it will do nothing for your personal health unless you act on it and actually exercise. And that’s the hard part. Reading an article about exercise is easy. Getting into an actual routine of regular exercise is harder.

(B) In this sense, science really solves no problems at all. Problems are only solved when people take the knowledge provided by science and use it. In fact, many of humanity’s biggest problems are caused by lack of action, and not lack of knowledge.

(C) That understanding alone solves no problems. Individual people have to act on that understanding for it to help solve problems. For instance, science has found that regular exercise can lower your risk of heart disease.
[선택형11~12] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Sound is produced through vibrations that occur from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar are played, for instance. ( A ) The vibrations of the sound source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when you throw a stone. ( B ) When these sound waves reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound. ( C ) Just as different ripples in water might overlap if you throw two stones, sound waves can also interfere with each other when they meet. ( D ) Constructive interference occurs when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a bigger wave and a louder sound. ( E ) Destructive interference, on the other hand, occurs when a peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound, or no sound at all.
윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.5점]
There are two types of interference: constructive and destructive.
① (A)     ② (B)     ③ (C)     ④ (D)     ⑤ (E)
윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
① The principle of how sound is produced and the interference between sound waves
② The characteristics of sounds produced by various musical instruments
③ How the brain distinguishes different types of sounds
④ The spreading of ripples and their visual similarity to sound waves
⑤ Ways to reduce noise in everyday life
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo’s mutated genes into “normal” ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
① Genetic Disorders and How to Prevent Them
② Why Babies Are Born with Genetic Problems
③ Changing Our Future: The Wonders of Genetic Science
④ Ethical Dilemmas of Gene Editing in Unborn Children
⑤ Building Smarter and Stronger Humans with Gene Editing
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

Stanford psychology professor Dr. Carol Dweck is the internationally recognized pioneer of the concept of “growth mindset” as a way to continually grow, learn, and persevere in our efforts. Dweck found that kids who are told they’re “smart” actually underperform in future tasks, by choosing easier tasks to avoid evidence that they are not smart, which Dweck calls having a “fixed mindset.” In contrast, Dweck found, kids who are praised not for their smarts but for their effort develop what Dweck calls a “growth mindset.” They learn that their effort is what led to their success, and if they continue to try, over time they’ll improve and achieve more things. These kids end up ____________________, and feel a greater sense of accomplishment. “Emphasizing effort gives a child a variable that they can control,” Dweck has explained.
① providing that they are smart
② taking on more demanding work
③ pursuing tasks with lower difficulty
④ overlooking the value of their effort
⑤ trusting in their innate cognitive abilities
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.1점]

Studies of experts provide insight into what it means to have deep and flexible understanding. ①Experts in a particular domain are people who have deep, richly interconnected ideas about the world. They are not just good thinkers or people who are exceptionally smart. Rather, experts have knowledge in a specific domain ─ such as chess, chemistry, or tennis ─ and are not generalists. ②Some experts tend to exhibit strong leadership skills in team-based environments. However, experts do not just know “a bunch of facts.” ③ln fact, having expertise in a topic means that knowledge is organized into coherent frameworks, and the expert understands the interrelationship between facts and can distinguish which ideas are most central. ④This kind of deep but organized understanding allows for greater flexibility in learning and facilitates application across multiple contexts. ⑤Such expertise enables experts to approach new problems more effectively and adapt their knowledge to unfamiliar situations.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]

What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, the author needs to build a positive ①connection between the protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be ②perceived as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions ③benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that ④provoke little audience reaction. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally ⑤uninvolved in a character as either ally or enemy.
다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]

Most entrepreneurs put in tremendous amounts of time and effort in creating and launching new products and services and then make the mistake of overpricing them. They have created something they care deeply about, it’s theirs, and this powerful sense of ownership distorts their perception of value which causes them to overprice their products. While many of them are quick to realize that their initial prices are too high, not all these people are happy or willing to drop their prices to make their products more attractive. And this can be a very costly mistake that may lead to the failure of their new business. When you launch a new product or service, your priority should be to get sufficient market adoption as soon as possible and you should be ready to sacrifice your initial prices and profits to achieve this aim. Once you have strong sales volumes, you can increase your prices to maximize your profits.

Entrepreneurs often overprice their new products due to emotional attachment, which distorts their perception of value and can (A)___________ market acceptance. To succeed long-term, it’s crucial to prioritize early market adoption─even if it means (B)___________ initial prices and profits─before setting higher prices later for greater profitability.
① facilitate	       sacrificing
② obstruct	       reducing
③ facilitate	       lowering
④ obstruct	       enhancing
⑤ hinder	       promoting
① increasing the number of drive-through lanes
② eliminating vehicle noise
③ greeting customers more politely
④ speeding up the cooking process
⑤ adjusting the temperature of the food
[선택형 23~24] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Destructive interference is used in the noise-cancelling feature of headphones when we listen to music. Inside the headphones are microphones and noise-cancelling circuitry. The microphones pick up sounds from the outside, and the circuitry analyzes them to produce opposite sound waves. (A) For example, if outside noise has a value of +1, the circuitry will generate an opposite noise of -1 and transmit it to the speakers. (B) This cancels out the unwanted sound even in noisy surroundings, so you can hear the music sound clearly without turning up the volume. (C) Furthermore, smartphones are now equipped with high-resolution cameras that can take professional-quality photos. However, it is not easy to entirely eliminate external noise with this technology. (D) To achieve full noise cancellation, the circuitry must convert the noise into digital data and instantly transmit the opposite sound to the speakers as soon as the noise reaches the microphones. (E) Therefore, this noise-cancellation technology is effective for predictable sounds like those of car engines and subways that occur regularly or over a period of time. However, it’s relatively less effective for inconsistent sounds such as those of people talking close to you.
윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.1점]
① (A)     ② (B)     ③ (C)     ④ (D)     ⑤ (E)
윗글에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [3.1점]
① The noise-cancelling circuit receives external noise and then produces the same waveform to improve sound quality.
② The noise-cancelling function is able to completely block out the sound of conversation heard at a short distance.
③ The noise-cancelling technology can analyze and eliminate all kinds of noise instantly.
④ The noise-cancelling circuit converts music into digital signals and sends them to cancel the noise.
⑤ Noise-cancelling headphones are more effective for predictable sounds.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 2개 고르면? [3.5점]

We are now at a point of unprecedented genetic, cultural, and environmental power as a species, and we are linked to ①nearly every other person on Earth. We ②are embodied individuals trapped within limited time, but we are also networked data streams, memories, and influencers, and part of a grander humanity. Our decisions today have far-reaching impacts that place a responsibility on us to become good ancestors, to take the long view and time travel forward to imagine the well-being of billions of people ③who lives will be lived in the world we are currently making. Centuries ago, leaders of the native North American Iroquois people ④creating “seven generation stewardship,” instructing people to consider the impact of every decision on their children, seven generations into the future. In the precious few decades that Earth is ours, while we enjoy the gardens ⑤planted by our ancestors, we must not steal the shade from our descendants.
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.5점]
This doesn’t imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don’t need them for this concrete form of thinking.

Let’s assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. ( ① ) This doesn’t necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. ( ② ) We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she’s currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. ( ③ ) To do this, in principle she doesn’t need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. ( ④) It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. ( ⑤ ) For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she’s capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities.
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

Noise-cancelling technology is not only used in music devices. Other fields also take advantage of this technology, such as ticket offices at tourist attractions which are often very noisy. Microphones are installed in ticket offices to detect external noise, and an opposite sound wave is generated and transmitted through a speaker, enabling the ticket agent to hear the customer’s voice clearly. Another area in which this technology is used is drive-through fast-food restaurants and coffee shops. They use noise-cancelling headsets to improve communication between employees and customers by ___________________________. These noise-cancelling headsets help drive-through employees take orders accurately. The same technology is also used for cars, whose audio systems generate waves to cancel out unpleasant sounds such as engine, wind, and road noise. Thanks to noise-cancelling devices, it is possible for drivers to focus on driving without being disturbed by distracting noises.
다음 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 각각 들어갈 적절한 표현만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 골라 쓰시오.  [4점, 부분점수 없음]

As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions and judging his or her emotions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child “Why do you feel sad?” and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she’s feeling sad about her parents’ arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she’s worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions, direct reference to your child’s emotions, or ignoring them can just make a child silent. It’s better to simply reflect what you notice. You can say ⓐ__________________________ rather than ⓑ__________________________, and wait for her response.
a. Why are you so upset?
b. Your shoulders dropped w￼hen you came in.
c. You’re just overreacting.
d. You didn’t eat much dinner.
e. I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital.
f. Come on, it’s not a big deal.
다음 글을 토대로 주어진 질문에 적절한 답이 되도록 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말을 주어진 글에서 변형없이 그대로 찾아 쓰시오. (ⓐ는 연이은 3단어, ⓑ는 연이은 5단어로 쓸 것) [6점, 각 3점]

To monitor our surroundings is to focus on what’s outside of ourselves: what we see, hear, smell, feel, and perhaps even taste. But sometimes what really marks a place is something less specific - a feeling within us. An interesting example emerged from a study of subway passenger behavior. Researchers trying to understand why people sit where they sit or stand where they stand in subway and metro trains examined the factors that shape the way riders used and navigated that space in different situations. One of their findings involved the reasons many riders like to plant themselves close to the train’s doors. Partly this was the obvious convenience of being able to exit more quickly. But it was shaped partly by a more abstract sensation - the desire to avoid the sometimes uncomfortable feeling of accidentally making eye contact with seated passengers. We can’t see feelings - but they’re very real, and they influence our experience of the world.
Q: Why might riders choose to stand near the doors even when there is space elsewhere?
A: It’s because they seek both to ⓐ__________ and to ⓑ__________ of making eye contact with seated passengers.
<보 기>
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]

Paying with plastic fundamentally changes the way we spend money, altering the calculus of our financial decisions. When you buy something with cash, the purchase involves an actual loss – your wallet is literally lighter. Credit cards, however, make the purchase abstract, so that you don’t really feel the downside of spending money. Brain-imaging experiments suggest that paying with credit cards actually reduces activity in the insula, a brain region associated with negative feelings. As George Loewenstein, a neuroeconomist at Carnegie Mellon, says, “The nature of credit cards ensures that your brain is anesthetized against the pain of payment.” Spending money doesn’t feel bad, so you spend more money.

Consider this experiment: Drazen Prelec and Duncan Simester, two business professors at MIT, organized a real-life, sealed-bid auction for tickets to a Boston Celtics game. Half the participants in the auction were informed that they had to pay with cash; the other half were told they had to pay with credit cards. Prelec and Simester then averaged the bids for the two different groups. It turns out that the average credit card bid was twice as high as the average cash bid. When people used their credit cards, their bids were much more careless. They no longer felt the need to limit their expenses.
① When you pay cash, you can feel the money leaving your hand.
② When you pay with plastic, the purchase is made abstract.
③ Brain-imaging experiments imply that paying with a credit card makes our insula excited.
④ Credit cards anesthetizethe pain of paying.
⑤ In the experiment of the Celtics auction, the average bid on a credit card was twice as high as the average cash bid.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 표현을 2개 골라 옳은 표현으로 수정하시오. [6점, 각 3점]

Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can’t force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used ⓐprovidng information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales ⓑgo up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long term effect of getting a consumer ⓒto buy something they did not really want or need wasn’t good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and ⓓpromote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the uninterested consumers are, and ⓔhow to reach them.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 the opposite is the case를 설명하는 내용이 되도록 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 각각 가장 적절한 한 단어를 쓰시오. (주어진 철자로 시작하는 단어를 쓸 것) [9점, 각 3점]

We think we’re being logical, objective, and rational – and therefore accurate in our analysis, judgment, and decisions. So we think that if other people are logical, objective, and rational, they will agree with us and see what we see. But the opposite is the case. Every human brain is different. Everyone’s life experience is different. Everyone’s desires and knowledge are different. You might think you’re being realistic – that is, that your ideas match reality, but that’s impossible. It’s only your interpretation of reality, which will always be different from someone else’s. When two nations play each other in the World Cup, the fans of each country criticize the referees for missing all the infractions that the other team commits. Without fail, each fan base believes that the referees are biased against their team.
We can’t see the picture that forms in the ⓐm___________ of the other person. So we can’t see if they see what we see about our ⓑi___________. Human perception is always ⓒs___________.
다음 우리말 표현과 같은 의미가 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 배열하시오. (단, 주어진 표현만 한 번씩 사용하며, 변형 금지)  [6점]
told / unattractive / have / anything / ￼of / will / require / doing / simply seems / that / you / patience / the prospect / been
우선 한 가지는, 인내심을 요구할 것이라고 들은 어떤 일을 여러분이 한다는 예상은 정말로 매력 없어 보인다.
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 말을 본문의 단어를 활용하여 쓰시오. [9점, 각 3점]

The emphasis on learning from the ingroup takes little account of individuals. Amazingly, while we may dislike some of the people in our ingroup, we still copy them. Wilks, Kirby, and Nielsen studied copying behavior in the context of observing how to open a puzzle box. Ingroups and outgroups were distinguished in a minimal way, using simple color coding of wristbands. The children did not simply like all members of their ingroup; they disliked those who behaved in an antisocial fashion. Indeed, they liked these antisocial ingroup members less than the prosocial members of an outgroup. Still, their dislike did not affect their tendency to copy ingroup behavior more closely than outgroup behavior. This overimitation reveals that we are not copying in order to learn how to open a box most efficiently. We want to learn how to do it in the proper way—in other words, conforming to the rules and conventions of the ingroup. This will be appropriately demonstrated even by antisocial ingroup members.

The study indicates that children’s ⓐ___________ to their group persists even when they observe ⓑ___________ individuals, as their primary goal is following social conventions rather than ⓒ___________.
- 한 칸당 하나의 단어를 적을 것￼
- 본문에 쓰인 단어만 사용할 것
- 필요시 단어의 형태를 어법에 맞게 변화시킬 것
<보 기>
<조 건>
